subject: DPA negotiation: definitions, telemetry & execution
messages:
From: Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@heliomed.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>
Cc: HelioMed Legal <contracts@heliomed.com>
Date: Thu, 12 Nov 2026 10:03:00 -0800
Subject: DPA questions re: roles, telemetry, embeddings (HelioMed)

Hi Marissa —

Thanks for the quick intro last week. Our procurement + privacy teams reviewed Redwood's standard DPA and sent a redline (attached). A few high-level items we need to align on before counsel can sign:

- Roles: we want explicit confirmation HelioMed is the controller and Redwood is the processor. If any parts of the service result in joint-determination, we need an explanatory note.
- Logs & telemetry: procurement is worried about prompt-level logs and whether those could include PHI. Need to confirm what is stored, retention, and access controls.
- Embeddings: are embeddings treated as "customer data" (not used for training) or can Redwood use derived embeddings for product improvements? If embeddings are considered pseudonymous, what protections apply?
- Subprocessors & transfers: we need current subprocessor list + confirmation of SCCs for EU transfers, and whether you accept UK Addendum/Swiss requirements.

Attached: HelioMed_DPA_Redline_v2.pdf (redline + comment threads). Can you review and send a consolidated redline? Also procurement prefers DocuSign for execution — we can accept that but need signer names and Azure AD SSO for procurement sign-off.

Thanks — happy to hop on a 30m call if easier.

Jordan
Legal Ops | HelioMed

(Attachment: HelioMed_DPA_Redline_v2.pdf)

From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>
To: Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@heliomed.com>
Cc: Neha Kapoor <neha_kapoor@redwood.ai>, Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.ai>
Date: Fri, 13 Nov 2026 09:14:00 -0800
Subject: Re: DPA questions re: roles, telemetry, embeddings (HelioMed)

Jordan —

Appreciate the detailed redline. I've looped in our privacy and legal partners (Neha + Laura) to align on language. High level response and proposed next steps below:

1) Roles: Redwood's standard position is: customer (HelioMed) = Controller; Redwood = Processor. We will add an explanatory clause stating Redwood may be a processor-only party; any joint-determination scenarios will be escalated to customer counsel before product changes.

2) Logs & telemetry: our default is to retain operational logs (request/response metadata, system traces) for 30 days for debugging and availability; logs containing full prompt/response payloads are truncated and encrypted; access is strictly role-based. For customers processing regulated data we offer extended retention controls and can add audit logging on request.

3) Embeddings: Redwood treats raw customer content and embeddings as Customer Data by default and does not use them to train models or improve product models. We can add explicit non-training and non-derivative-use language for embeddings.

4) Subprocessors and transfers: we'll provide an up-to-date subprocessor list (attached) and commit to 30 days' notice for new subprocessors. For EU transfers we rely on SCCs, and we can accept the UK Addendum and Swiss requirements as a standard addendum.

Next steps I propose:
- Laura to provide suggested clause language for logs/telemetry and embeddings.
- We will produce a consolidated redline (attached) and a short playbook of our standard fallback language we are willing to accept.
- If that looks good, we can send the final DPA via DocuSign. Please confirm the signers and whether Azure AD SSO is required for procurement.

Attaching: Redwood_DPA_Redline_v3.pdf, Redwood_Subprocessor_List.csv

Happy to jump on the call — propose Monday 11/16 if that works for you.

Best,
Marissa Cole
Head of Strategic Accounts | Redwood Inference

(Attachments: Redwood_DPA_Redline_v3.pdf, Redwood_Subprocessor_List.csv)

From: Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@heliomed.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>
Date: Mon, 15 Nov 2026 08:22:00 -0800
Subject: Re: DPA questions re: roles, telemetry, embeddings (HelioMed)

Marissa —

Thanks for the fast turnaround and attachments. A couple quick clarifications before counsel reviews your consolidated redline:

- Embeddings: when you say "treated as Customer Data," does that include prevention of substring re-identification in model caches/logs? Our privacy team is specifically concerned about whether embeddings or small prompt fragments are ever stored in plain text or reversible form.
- Telemetry: does "request/response metadata" include prompt-level timings and truncated prompt text? Procurement would prefer metadata only unless there is an operational incident that requires full payload retention.

Procurement confirms: DocuSign is fine, and they do require Azure AD-based SSO for signer verification. Signer for HelioMed will be: Jordan Blake (Legal Ops) and Amelia Park (VP Procurement).

If you can add clarifying language around non-reversible storage for embeddings and metadata-only telemetry as the default, we can circulate to counsel.

Jordan

From: Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.ai>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>, Neha Kapoor <neha_kapoor@redwood.ai>, Rishi Malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.ai>
Date: Mon, 15 Nov 2026 10:05:00 -0800
Subject: Internal: suggested DPA language + negotiation playbook (do not forward)

Marissa / Neha / Rishi —

Below are suggested snippets you can propose back to HelioMed. Keep the public-facing email concise; the legal rationale is below each snippet if asked.

Snippet A — Roles (controller/processor):
"HelioMed is the Controller and Redwood Inference, Inc. is the Processor with respect to Customer Data submitted through the Services. In instances where the Parties are required to determine purposes and means jointly, the Parties shall notify each other and negotiate in good faith to document the respective responsibilities."
Rationale: preserves our position but commits to cooperation if product use cases blur lines.

Snippet B — Embeddings / Training:
"Redwood will treat embeddings and any derived representations of Customer Data as Customer Data and will not use them to train, improve, or benchmark Redwood's underlying models or products, except with Customer's explicit written consent. Embeddings will be stored in a non-reversible format where feasible; any reversible caches will be encrypted and access-restricted."
Rationale: addresses re-identification concerns directly.

Snippet C — Logs & telemetry (default):
"Default telemetry shall consist of anonymized operational metadata (timestamps, latency, model-id, token counts) and truncated, non-user-identifying request identifiers. Full request/response payloads shall not be retained beyond 30 days except for debugging under a documented incident process and only with Customer admin consent. Customers requiring different retention or audit access may request a contract amendment."
Rationale: balances operational needs with privacy. We can offer 45 days as an alternative for enterprise if necessary.

Snippet D — Subprocessors & transfers:
"Redwood will maintain an up-to-date list of subprocessors at the link provided and will give Customer at least 30 days' notice of any new subprocessor engaged to process Customer Data. International transfers shall be governed by appropriate transfer mechanisms (e.g., EU SCCs, UK Addendum) as required."
Rationale: standard market language.

Operational notes: accept Azure AD SSO requirement for DocuSign signer verification. If HelioMed insists on zero reversible storage of embeddings we should ask for limited operational carveouts (encrypted caches) and the right to debug with Customer authorization.

If you want, I can push the snippets into the redline and produce a one-page negotiation playbook for Marissa to send.

Laura
Head of Privacy | Redwood Inference

From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>
To: Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@heliomed.com>, HelioMed Legal <contracts@heliomed.com>
Cc: Neha Kapoor <neha_kapoor@redwood.ai>, Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.ai>, Rishi Malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.ai>
Date: Mon, 15 Nov 2026 16:42:00 -0800
Subject: Final redline + DocuSign link (ready for signature)

Jordan / HelioMed team —

Thanks — we've incorporated the suggested language (see excerpts below) and updated the consolidated redline. Key points:

- Roles: explicit controller/processor language + notification path for joint-determination.
- Embeddings: now explicitly treated as Customer Data; non-training and non-derivative-use clause added; storage described as non-reversible where feasible and encrypted in caches.
- Telemetry: default is metadata-only (timestamps, latency, token counts, model-id). Full payload retention limited to 30 days and only for debugging under an incident process; we offered 45 days as an enterprise option.
- Subprocessors & transfers: latest list attached; we accept SCCs + UK Addendum; 30-day notice for changes.

Attachments: Redwood_DPA_Redline_v3.pdf, Redwood_Subprocessor_List.csv
DocuSign envelope: https://docusign.com/HelioMed-Redwood-DPA-Envelope-12345

Signers we will expect on your side: Jordan Blake (Legal Ops) and Amelia Park (VP Procurement). We will use Azure AD SSO for signer verification per your procurement requirement.

If that all looks good please sign via the DocuSign link and I will countersign on behalf of Redwood. If you'd like a final 15m walkthrough of the redline, happy to set that up.

Best,
Marissa Cole
Head of Strategic Accounts | Redwood Inference

(Attachments: Redwood_DPA_Redline_v3.pdf, Redwood_Subprocessor_List.csv)
